findings.reason: as written the claim and the mechanism disagree on one of the four named routes, so a worker implements whole-string refusal and the section's own acceptance promise is false for it, or the section must state that the `set body` route refuses a legacy body and the escape is a text-mode edit.
findings.text: §4 states "Text already in a plan is never refused. Only the fragment a write adds is checked, so editing an old plan stays possible", but the mechanism it names checks the whole string a path supplies: `_store_section_ops._require_authored_value` passes the new body alone to `_refuse_forged_structure` (`reckon/_store_section_ops.py:143-144`) with no prior body to diff against, and `_insert_authored_section` likewise checks `request["body"]` whole (`reckon/_store.py:941-946`), so a `set` that re-writes a legacy section body whose prose already carries the term is refused even though it adds nothing, while §1 records that legacy plan sections do carry the term in a paragraph — the claim holds only for the text-mode route, where the write supplies an `old_html`/`new_html` pair and the delta is localisable

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the predicate at `reckon/_store.py:899` and its refuser at `:924`, `_queue_authored_section` at `:3371`, `insert_section`/`append_evidence` calls at `:946`/`:1074`, `_store_section_ops._refuse_forged_structure` at `:124`, `doccheck._prose_text` at `:385` and `_plan_html.section_prose` at `:474` all resolve as cited, and `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS` at `:2303` is `{script, style, head}` exactly as the section says.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §4's eight cases each name an observable refusal or acceptance through a named channel (`op_error`, `text_edit_error`), and the section declares a negative control (remove the check, and the first case is accepted) exercised at base and head against every test file that drives the three routes.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate writes `docs/evidence/fragments/additional-work-is-a-section/a-plan-write-refuses-the-bucket.html` in the repository, not a scratch or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name or ticket number reaches a proposed symbol or file; `tests/test_a_plan_write_refuses_the_bucket.py` names the guard by what it does.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §4's principle that text already in a plan is never refused does not hold for the `set sections.<id>.body` route its own mechanism names.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the store refusal and the `audit-doc` warning are one guard read at two surfaces (write time and audit), the section states that explicitly, and a single verdict closes both.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §4 declares no dependency and needs none: it writes the store, the section-ops module and the doc-check module, none of which §2 or §3 touch, and the plan's own `plan-section-depends-on` (`s5` → `s2`,`s3`,`s4`) already places §5 after it.
